vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — ninth consecutive session (Friday June 26 through Saturday July 4 morning). July 4 morning: the Vibe 4 baseline holds across the holiday with no overnight escalation triggering either direction. The July 4 federal holiday reduces the observability window on multiple tracks — SNSC formal action by Iranian authorities is structurally less likely during a US federal holiday; markets are closed removing the real-time economic price signal; and government communications cadence is reduced. Active positives Saturday morning: (a) Lebanon Fragile Hold advances to Day 7 of Hezbollah 'null and void' political rejection without military resumption — seven consecutive days of political non-compliance without operational resumption is the ceasefire period's most sustained post-rejection durability signal to date; (b) Doha follow-on track remains active — both sides agreed to continue discussions following the July 1-2 round; (c) Hamilton Fire near Winthrop approaching full containment (90%+); (d) Tule Road Fire near Toppenish advancing toward full containment (95%); (e) Measles extended surveillance Day 5 clean — no new clusters from either Lumen Field exposure window; (f) L-Pod orca calf advances to Week 10 alive; (g) Goldman Sachs formally retracted 'lost decade' market call, signaling improved long-run equity confidence. Active negatives Saturday morning: (a) SNSC compliance Day 16 — the 60-day nuclear clock advances while the SNSC formal position change remains unissued; Iran's post-Doha corridor sovereignty assertion and cargo strike remain unaddressed, keeping the Lloyd's gate formally closed; 118 tankers remain commercially stranded; (b) July 4 peak compound ignition risk window FULLY ACTIVE — Tucannon Fire Day 7 at 30,000+ acres with Level 3 evacuations, second heat wave Day 4 at maximum fuel dryness amplification, and human ignition overlay (holiday fireworks and recreation) converging simultaneously; (c) Russia fuel crisis Day 4 — 2/3 of federal entities rationing with IEA 'unprecedented' designation standing; escalation trajectory over four days indicates spreading lateral distribution failure; (d) Extreme heat threatening America 250 celebrations — DC heat index ~107°F; Great American State Fair temporarily closed; events scaled back; wildfire compound risk elevated by same heat event nationally; (e) OBBB Day 4 with CMS guidance still unpublished — state readiness gap accumulating; OR/WA 3.6M enrollees without comprehensive documentation; (f) Acting DNI Day 45 — ninth week — at maximum monitoring demand. Vibe 5 recovery triggers: SNSC formal compliance retraction or written compliance statement (unlocks Lloyd's gate; releases 118-tanker backlog; WTI supply pulse); Lebanon Hezbollah military command acceptance of ceasefire framework; Tucannon significant containment progress through July 4 holiday weekend; June CPI July 14 decelerating toward 3.5% range (reduces dual-mandate tension; October hike probability compresses further). Vibe 3 triggers: SNSC formal re-escalation or new CENTCOM engagement; Lebanon formal void declaration or Hezbollah rocket resumption; Tucannon catastrophic holiday weekend run to 50,000+ acres; Russian fuel crisis producing confirmed military logistics attrition in Zaporizhzhia or Kupyansk corridors. None triggered Saturday July 4 morning.

items.summary: The Hormuz compliance architecture enters July 4 morning at Day 16 of the SNSC formal review period with no overnight movement on any of the critical gate indicators: the SNSC formal re-closure retraction remains unissued; Iran's physical cargo strike on the IMO-backed Oman route vessel (June 26) remains unaddressed at Day 9; the Lloyd's war-risk normalization gate remains formally closed. The July 4 US federal holiday structurally reduces the probability of Iranian administrative action today — the SNSC is a domestic Iranian governance body not operationally bound by US holiday calendars, but prior pattern in this series has shown formal compliance determinations clustering around active US-Iran diplomatic engagement sessions. With Doha follow-on talks in the queue rather than in session today, July 4 is analytically quiet on the SNSC track. The Doha July 1-2 round's formal conclusion with Qatar's 'positive progress' designation established the operative diplomatic baseline: both sides agreed to continue discussions; the round covered Hormuz maritime transit normalization and unfreezing of Iranian assets; no written compliance statement was produced. Iran's post-Doha posture continues to assert joint sovereign corridor control with Oman — a governance position that exceeds the pre-conflict baseline and that Iran is not walking back even while diplomatic engagement continues. The 118 tankers commercially stranded pending Lloyd's gate normalization remain the structural negative metric. Physical Hormuz traffic continues building through the CENTCOM corridor; demining progress on the approximately 80 remaining central-channel mines continues. WTI crude oil enters Saturday's holiday session in the approximately $67-70 range — thin holiday trading with no substantive price discovery expected today. The 60-day nuclear clock advances to Day 16 with approximately 44 days remaining through approximately August 18. Trump stated the 60-day window is 'not a hard deadline' and 'could take longer.' Working groups on nuclear inspections and sanctions formed but nothing substantive yet negotiated on the nuclear programme. Lebanon: Hezbollah's 'null and void' rejection of the Rubio ceasefire framework advances to Day 7 — seven consecutive days of political non-compliance without operational resumption of hostilities. No formal void declaration has been issued. IDF drone activity in the southern Lebanon buffer zone continues. The Lebanon Fragile Hold durability signal is the most sustained post-rejection hold of the ceasefire period.

Three federal wildland firefighters were killed in the June 27 Colorado-Utah burnover. NIFC Preparedness Level 3 advances to Day 18.

analyst_summary: July 4, 2026 — America's 250th birthday — opens at Vibe 4, the ninth consecutive session at this level (Friday June 26 through Saturday July 4 morning). The semiquincentennial arrives in a characteristic DVC brief cycle configuration: structurally ambiguous, with active positives and active negatives balancing to a mid-range assessment rather than resolving to either stability or crisis. The dominant geopolitical thread remains the SNSC compliance architecture: Hormuz Day 127 advances with the Iran SNSC formally unresolved at Day 16, Doha 'positive progress' established but no Lloyd's gate movement produced, and Iran asserting joint corridor control with Oman that exceeds the pre-conflict baseline. The July 4 federal holiday structurally reduces the probability of a formal Iranian SNSC action today — prior pattern in this series shows formal compliance determinations clustering around active diplomatic engagement sessions rather than quiet national holiday windows. The Lebanon Fragile Hold at Hour ~283+ and seven consecutive days of Hezbollah political rejection without military resumption is the most sustained post-rejection durability signal of the ceasefire period — a quiet positive that has not yet generated a Vibe 5 trigger but has materially reduced the daily risk floor. Russia's fuel crisis Day 4 — IEA 'unprecedented' designation standing, 2/3 of federal entities rationing, Kapotnya offline through year end, Kazakhstan imports in negotiation — represents the week's primary escalation track outside the Hormuz architecture. The July 4 PNW compound ignition risk window now fully active is the morning brief's most operationally urgent near-term concern: four simultaneous risk factors — Tucannon Fire Day 7 at 30,000+ acres with Level 3 evacuations, second heat wave Day 4 at record fuel dryness amplification, and human ignition overlay now live — create the highest compound-risk configuration of the East Cascades onset season. The Hamilton Fire's near-full containment and Tule Road's 95% containment provide partial resource offset, but the national reserve remains at the onset-period low. America's 250th birthday itself is a day of maximum domestic political theater: Freedom 250's National Mall fireworks (850,000 effects, world-record attempt, 7 PM) proceeds under a ~107°F heat index that has already forced the Great American State Fair's temporary closure and Philadelphia's parade cancellation. The OBBB's Day 4 implementation with CMS guidance still unpublished, and three-track election disruption at Day 5 with holiday pause expected, hold their current trajectories. The week ahead: SpaceX Nasdaq-100 live Monday (T-2); de minimis comment period close Sunday; FERC AI Large Load T-12; June CPI July 14 (decisive FOMC input); FOMC July 29. The 60-day nuclear clock at Day 16 with 44 days remaining to approximately August 18 is the primary geopolitical clock to monitor as the holiday weekend concludes.
